results.subject: GLM-5.2
results.artifact: General-R0 + lm_head/embed_tokens native protection (282 shards, 86.74GB, 0.921099 whole-model BPW)
results.methodology: Diagnosed from data already on disk at zero re-fetch cost: the packers own per-tensor relative_frobenius_error field showed lm_head=0.965 and embed_tokens=0.823 at R0, both COMPRESSIBLE_CANDIDATE, both far worse than every other category (attention/dense_mlp/shared_expert/routed_expert all 0.62-0.65). Re-fetched only the one shard both tensors live in (5.3GB, not 1.5TB), reclassified them PROTECTED_SOURCE_NATIVE (bf16), left the other 281 shards and all other tensors in shard 1 untouched. Cost: +3.6GB (0.883 -> 0.921 whole-model BPW), nowhere near the H10=1.0 uniform ceiling.

evidence.greedy_continuation_observed: 3 consecutive identical tokens (id 126218, a Chinese-language token '是实现')
evidence.note: Still collapses, on a DIFFERENT stuck token than either the malformed-prompt run (id 74242) or the correctly-formatted R0-alone run (id 73810). The specific failure token moves with any change to the artifact, but the fixed-point COLLAPSE PATTERN itself does not -- ruling out lm_head/embed_tokens reconstruction as a sufficient explanation on its own, though the 0.965/0.823 error was real and worth fixing regardless.

results.interpretation: The dominant remaining candidate is routed_expert compression: 97.5% of logical weight mass, relative_frobenius_error ~0.62 at R0 (much better than lm_head but still substantial), packed at the SAME geometry across all 256 experts x 78 layers. Prometheus general-v1 -- already built, already profiled this session -- specifies routed_expert/shared_expert/attention/dense_mlp at tier T1 = num8/den8 = exactly 1.0 BPW (H10), not R0 own 0.876-0.883. That gap, compounding over 78 layers on 97.5% of the model, is the leading unexplained factor.
results.consequence: A real fix now needs H10-equivalent packing (new geometry: dim=8/k=256, unimplemented) applied across essentially the WHOLE model, since routed_expert is 97.5% of the mass -- this is a full-scale re-fetch+re-pack (~1.5TB), not a small pilot. The two single-shard experiments already run were the correctly-scoped cheap tests before that commitment, and both are now spent.

results.subject: GLM-5.2
results.note: See GLM52_R1_GEOMETRY_INVALID_FINDING.json for full detail. Summary: no gravity-pq geometry strictly between R0 (0.875 nominal bpw) and BPW_CEILING=1.0 is admissible across GLM-5.2 T1-tier tensor sizes (routed_expert 12.58M, attention as small as 3.5M, dense_mlp up to 75.5M elements). A candidate (dim=11,k=1024) was tried and found to silently fail: _pq_geometry() requires a power-of-2 dim and falls back without error when given one that is not, producing meaningless per-tensor bpw. Corrected search confirms R0 is at or extremely near this codec familys practical ceiling for GLM-5.2s tensor shapes.
results.consequence: Bracketing upward via a new PQ rung (H10/H12/H15 per campaign S3.3) is not achievable within gravity-pq (S=1, power-of-2 dim) for routed_expert at GLM-5.2 scale. The only remaining levers inside the sub-bit-first LAW are protecting more categories natively (expensive, already tried on the two worst tensors, did not fix the collapse) or a different non-PQ codec. Crossing BPW_CEILING=1.0 needs a formal Escape Receipt -- a policy reversal of this projects sub-bit-first LAW, not an engineering choice, and is not invoked here without explicit authorization.

selection_gate: M03: R0 (0.883-0.921bpw depending on native-protection extent) is the practical ceiling of the current codec for GLM-5.2 and does not pass the screening gate. No higher uniform or near-uniform PQ rate exists to bracket to. Escape Receipt (crossing BPW_CEILING) or a different codec would be required for further recovery; neither is invoked without explicit authorization.
